verses.zh: 尼布甲尼撒在位第二年，他做了梦，心里烦乱，不能睡觉。
verses.en: In the second year of his[NOTE:1] reign Nebuchadnezzar had many dreams.[NOTE:2] His mind[NOTE:3] was disturbed, and he suffered from insomnia.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “Nebuchadnezzar’s.” The possessive pronoun is substituted in the translation for stylistic reasons.

Heb “dreamed dreams.” The plural is used here and in v. 2, but the singular in v. 3. The plural “dreams” has been variously explained. Some interpreters take the plural as denoting an indefinite singular (so GKC 400 §124.o). But it may be that it is describing a stream of related dreams, or a dream state. In the latter case, one might translate: “Nebuchadnezzar was in a trance.” See further, J. A. Montgomery, Daniel (ICC), 142.
Heb “his spirit.”

Heb “his sleep left (?) him.” The use of the verb הָיָה (hayah, “to be”) here is unusual. The context suggests a meaning such as “to be finished” or “gone” (cf. Dan 8:27). Some scholars emend the verb to read נָדְדָה (nadedah, “fled”); cf. Dan 6:19. See further, DCH 2:540 s.v. היה I Ni.3; HALOT 244 s.v. היה nif; BDB 227-28 s.v. הָיָה Niph.2.

verses.zh: 王吩咐人将术士、用法术的、行邪术的，和迦勒底人召来，要他们将王的梦告诉王，他们就来站在王前。
verses.en: The king issued an order[NOTE:1] to summon the magicians, astrologers, sorcerers, and wise men[NOTE:2] in order to explain his dreams to him.[NOTE:3] So they came and awaited the king’s instructions.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “said.” So also in v. 12.
Heb “Chaldeans.” The term Chaldeans (Hebrew כַּשְׂדִּים, kasdim) is used in the book of Daniel both in an ethnic sense and, as here, to refer to a caste of Babylonian wise men and astrologers.
Heb “to explain to the king his dreams.”
Heb “stood before the king.”

verses.zh: 王对他们说：「我做了一梦，心里烦乱，要知道这是甚么梦。」
verses.en: The king told them, “I have had a dream,[NOTE:1] and I[NOTE:2] am anxious to understand the dream.”
notes: Heb “I have dreamed a dream” (so KJV, ASV).
Heb “my spirit.”

verses.zh: 迦勒底人用亚兰的言语对王说：「愿王万岁！请将那梦告诉仆人，仆人就可以讲解。」
verses.en: The wise men replied to the king: [What follows is in Aramaic[NOTE:1]] “O king, live forever! Tell your servants the dream, and we will disclose its[NOTE:2] interpretation.”
notes: Contrary to common belief, the point here is not that the wise men (Chaldeans) replied to the king in the Aramaic language, or that this language was uniquely the language of the Chaldeans. It was this view that led in the past to Aramaic being referred to as “Chaldee.” Aramaic was used as a lingua franca during this period; its origins and usage were not restricted to the Babylonians. Rather, this phrase is better understood as an editorial note (cf. NAB) marking the fact that from 2:4b through 7:28 the language of the book shifts from Hebrew to Aramaic. In 8:1, and for the remainder of the book, the language returns to Hebrew. Various views have been advanced to account for this change of language, most of which are unconvincing. The change in language likely reflects stages in the transmission history of the book of Daniel or factors in its composition history.
Or “the.”

verses.zh: 王回答迦勒底人说：「梦我已经忘了（或译：我已定命；八节同），你们若不将梦和梦的讲解告诉我，就必被凌迟，你们的房屋必成为粪堆；
verses.en: The king replied[NOTE:1] to the wise men, “My decision is firm.[NOTE:2] If you do not inform me of both the dream and its interpretation, you will be dismembered[NOTE:3] and your homes reduced to rubble!
notes: Aram “answered and said,” a common idiom to indicate a reply, but redundant in contemporary English.

It seems clear from what follows that Nebuchadnezzar clearly recalls the content of the dream, although obviously he does not know what to make of it. By not divulging the dream itself to the would-be interpreters, he intends to find out whether they are simply leading him on. If they can tell him the dream’s content, which he is able to verify, he then can have confidence in their interpretation, which is what eludes him. The translation “the matter is gone from me” (cf. KJV, ASV), suggesting that the king had simply forgotten the dream, is incorrect. The Aramaic word used here (אַזְדָּא, ʾazdaʾ) is probably of Persian origin; it occurs in the OT only here and in v. 8. There are two main possibilities for the meaning of the word: “the matter is promulgated by me” (see KBL 1048 s.v.) and therefore “publicly known” (cf. NRSV; F. Rosenthal, Grammar, 62-63, §189), or “the matter is irrevocable” (cf. NAB, NIV, TEV, CEV, NLT; HALOT 1808 s.v. אזד; cf. also BDB 1079 s.v.). The present translation reflects this latter option. See further E. Vogt, Lexicon linguae aramaicae, 3.
Aram “made limbs” (cf. 3:29).

verses.zh: 你们若将梦和梦的讲解告诉我，就必从我这里得赠品和赏赐，并大尊荣。现在你们要将梦和梦的讲解告诉我。」
verses.en: But if you can disclose the dream and its interpretation, you will receive from me gifts, a reward, and considerable honor. So disclose to me the dream and its interpretation.”

verses.zh: 他们第二次对王说：「请王将梦告诉仆人，仆人就可以讲解。」
verses.en: They again replied, “Let the king inform us[NOTE:1] of the dream; then we will disclose its[NOTE:2] interpretation.”
notes: Aram “his servants.”
Or “the.”

verses.zh: 王回答说：「我准知道你们是故意迟延，因为你们知道那梦我已经忘了。
verses.en: The king replied, “I know for sure that you are attempting to gain time, because you see that my decision is firm.

verses.zh: 你们若不将梦告诉我，只有一法待你们；因为你们预备了谎言乱语向我说，要等候时势改变。现在你们要将梦告诉我，因我知道你们能将梦的讲解告诉我。」
verses.en: If you don’t inform me of the dream, there is only one thing that is going to happen to you.[NOTE:1] For you have agreed among yourselves to report to me something false and deceitful[NOTE:2] until such time as things might change. So tell me the dream, and I will have confidence[NOTE:3] that you can disclose its interpretation.”
notes: Aram “one is your law,” i.e., only one thing is applicable to you.
Aram “a lying and corrupt word.”
Aram “I will know.”

verses.zh: 迦勒底人在王面前回答说：「世上没有人能将王所问的事说出来；因为没有君王、大臣、掌权的向术士，或用法术的，或迦勒底人问过这样的事。
verses.en: The wise men replied to the king, “There is no man on earth who is able to disclose the king’s secret,[NOTE:1] for no king, regardless of his position and power, has ever requested such a thing from any magician, astrologer, or wise man.
notes: Aram “matter, thing.”

verses.zh: 王所问的事甚难。除了不与世人同居的神明，没有人在王面前能说出来。」
verses.en: What the king is asking is too difficult, and no one exists who can disclose it to the king, except for the gods—but they don’t live among mortals!”[NOTE:1]
notes: Aram “whose dwelling is not with flesh.”

verses.zh: 因此，王气忿忿地大发烈怒，吩咐灭绝巴比伦所有的哲士。
verses.en: Because of this the king got furiously angry[NOTE:1] and gave orders to destroy all the wise men of Babylon.
notes: Aram “was angry and very furious.” The expression is a hendiadys (two words or phrases expressing a single idea).

verses.zh: 于是命令发出，哲士将要见杀，人就寻找但以理和他的同伴，要杀他们。
verses.en: So a decree went out, and the wise men were about[NOTE:1] to be executed. They also sought[NOTE:2] Daniel and his friends so that they could be executed.
notes: The Aramaic participle is used here to express the imminent future.
The impersonal active plural (“they sought”) of the Aramaic verb could also be translated as an English passive: “Daniel and his friends were sought” (cf. NAB).

verses.zh: 王的护卫长亚略出来，要杀巴比伦的哲士，但以理就用婉言回答他，
verses.en: Then Daniel spoke with prudent counsel[NOTE:1] to Arioch, who was in charge of the king’s executioners and who had gone out to execute the wise men of Babylon.
notes: Aram “returned prudence and counsel.” The expression is a hendiadys.

verses.zh: 向王的护卫长亚略说：「王的命令为何这样紧急呢？」亚略就将情节告诉但以理。
verses.en: He inquired of Arioch the king’s deputy, “Why is the decree from the king so urgent?”[NOTE:1] Then Arioch informed Daniel about the matter.
notes: The Aramaic word מְהַחְצְפָה (mehakhtsefah) may refer to the severity of the king’s decree (i.e., “harsh”; so HALOT 1879 s.v. חצף; BDB 1093 s.v. חֲצַף), although it would seem that in a delicate situation such as this Daniel would avoid this kind of criticism of the king’s actions. The translation above understands the word to refer to the immediacy, not harshness, of the decree. See further, F. Rosenthal, Grammar, 50, §116; E. Vogt, Lexicon linguae aramaicae, 67.

verses.zh: 但以理遂进去求王宽限，就可以将梦的讲解告诉王。
verses.en: So Daniel went in and[NOTE:1] requested the king to grant him time, that he might disclose the interpretation to the king.
notes: Theodotion and the Syriac lack the words “went in and.”

verses.zh: 但以理回到他的居所，将这事告诉他的同伴哈拿尼雅、米沙利、亚撒利雅，
verses.en: Then Daniel went to his home and informed his friends Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah of the matter.

verses.zh: 要他们祈求天上的　神施怜悯，将这奥秘的事指明，免得但以理和他的同伴与巴比伦其余的哲士一同灭亡。
verses.en: He asked them to pray for mercy from the God of heaven concerning this mystery so that he[NOTE:1] and his friends would not be destroyed along with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.
notes: Aram “Daniel.” The proper name is redundant here in English and has not been included in the translation.

verses.zh: 这奥秘的事就在夜间异象中给但以理显明，但以理便称颂天上的　神。
verses.en: Then in a night vision the mystery was revealed to Daniel. So Daniel praised[NOTE:1] the God of heaven,
notes: Or “blessed.”

verses.zh: 但以理说：「　神的名是应当称颂的！从亘古直到永远，因为智慧能力都属乎他。
verses.en: saying:[NOTE:1] “Let the name of God[NOTE:2] be praised[NOTE:3] forever and ever,for wisdom and power belong to him.
notes: Aram “Daniel answered and said.”
As is often the case in the Bible, here the name represents the person.
Or “blessed.”

verses.zh: 他改变时候、日期，废王，立王，将智慧赐与智慧人，将知识赐与聪明人。
verses.en: He changes times and seasons,deposing some kings and establishing others.[NOTE:1] He gives wisdom to the wise;he imparts knowledge to those with understanding;[NOTE:2]
notes: Aram “kings.”
Aram “the knowers of understanding.”

verses.zh: 他显明深奥隐秘的事，知道暗中所有的，光明也与他同居。
verses.en: he reveals deep and hidden things.He knows what is in the darkness,and light resides with him.

verses.zh: 我列祖的　神啊，我感谢你，赞美你，因你将智慧才能赐给我，允准我们所求的，把王的事给我们指明。」
verses.en: O God of my fathers, I acknowledge and glorify you,for you have bestowed wisdom and power on me.Now you have enabled me to understand what we[NOTE:1] requested from you.For you have enabled us to understand the king’s dilemma.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Various explanations have been offered for the plurals we and us. They could be editorial plurals, or refer to Daniel and his three friends who were also praying about the matter.
Aram “the word of the king.”

verses.zh: 于是，但以理进去见亚略，就是王所派灭绝巴比伦哲士的，对他说：「不要灭绝巴比伦的哲士，求你领我到王面前，我要将梦的讲解告诉王。」
verses.en: Then Daniel went in to see[NOTE:1] Arioch (whom the king had appointed to destroy the wise men of Babylon). He came[NOTE:2] and said to him, “Don’t destroy the wise men of Babylon! Escort me[NOTE:3] to the king, and I will disclose the interpretation to him.”[NOTE:4]
notes: The MT has עַל עַל (ʿal ʿal, “he entered upon”). Several medieval Hebrew MSS lack the verb, although this may be due to haplography.
The LXX and Vulgate, along with one medieval Hebrew MS, lack this verb.
Aram “cause me to enter,” as also in v. 25.
Aram “the king.”

verses.zh: 亚略就急忙将但以理领到王面前，对王说：「我在被掳的犹大人中遇见一人，他能将梦的讲解告诉王。」
verses.en: So Arioch quickly ushered Daniel into the king’s presence, saying to him, “I[NOTE:1] have found a man from the captives of Judah who can make known the interpretation to the king.”
notes: Arioch’s claim is self-serving and exaggerated. It is Daniel who came to him, and not the other way around. By claiming to have found one capable of solving the king’s dilemma, Arioch probably hoped to ingratiate himself to the king.

verses.zh: 王问称为伯提沙撒的但以理说：「你能将我所做的梦和梦的讲解告诉我吗？」
verses.en: The king then asked Daniel (whose name was also Belteshazzar), “Are you able to make known to me the dream that I saw, as well as its interpretation?”

verses.zh: 但以理在王面前回答说：「王所问的那奥秘事，哲士、用法术的、术士、观兆的都不能告诉王；
verses.en: Daniel replied to the king, “The mystery that the king is asking about is such that no wise men, astrologers, magicians, or diviners can possibly disclose it to the king.

verses.zh: 只有一位在天上的　神能显明奥秘的事。他已将日后必有的事指示尼布甲尼撒王。你的梦和你在床上脑中的异象是这样：
verses.en: However, there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries,[NOTE:1] and he has made known to King Nebuchadnezzar what will happen in the times to come.[NOTE:2] The dream and the visions you had while lying on your bed[NOTE:3] are as follows:
notes: Aram “a revealer of mysteries.” The phrase serves as a quasi-title for God in Daniel.
Aram “in the latter days.”
Aram “your dream and the visions of your head upon your bed.”

verses.zh: 王啊，你在床上想到后来的事，那显明奥秘事的主把将来必有的事指示你。
verses.en: “As for you, O king, while you were in your bed your thoughts turned to future things.[NOTE:1] The revealer of mysteries has made known to you what will take place.
notes: Aram “your thoughts upon your bed went up to what will be after this.”

verses.zh: 至于那奥秘的事显明给我，并非因我的智慧胜过一切活人，乃为使王知道梦的讲解和心里的思念。
verses.en: As for me, this mystery was revealed to me not because I possess more wisdom[NOTE:1] than any other living person, but so that the king may understand[NOTE:2] the interpretation and comprehend the thoughts of your mind.[NOTE:3]
notes: Aram “not for any wisdom which is in me more than [in] any living man.”

Aram “they might cause the king to know.” The impersonal plural is used here to refer to the role of God’s spirit in revealing the dream and its interpretation to the king. As J. A. Montgomery says, “it appropriately here veils the mysterious agency” (Daniel [ICC], 164-65). Subsequent narratives show both God and angels involved with Nebuchadnezzar, so “they” can be appropriate.
Aram “heart.”

verses.zh: 「王啊，你梦见一个大像，这像甚高，极其光耀，站在你面前，形状甚是可怕。
verses.en: “You, O king, were watching as a great statue—one[NOTE:1] of impressive size and extraordinary brightness—was standing before you. Its appearance caused alarm.
notes: Aram “an image.”

verses.zh: 这像的头是精金的，胸膛和膀臂是银的，肚腹和腰是铜的，
verses.en: As for that statue, its head was of fine gold, its chest and arms were of silver, its belly and thighs were of bronze.

verses.zh: 腿是铁的，脚是半铁半泥的。
verses.en: Its legs were of iron; its feet were partly of iron and partly of clay.[NOTE:1]
notes: Clay refers to baked clay, which despite being hard was also fragile. Compare the reference in v. 41 to “wet clay.”

verses.zh: 你观看，见有一块非人手凿出来的石头打在这像半铁半泥的脚上，把脚砸碎；
verses.en: You were watching as[NOTE:1] a stone was cut out,[NOTE:2] but not by human hands. It struck the statue on its iron and clay feet, breaking them in pieces.
notes: Aram “until.”
The LXX, Theodotion, and the Vulgate have “from a mountain,” though this is probably a harmonization with v. 45.

verses.zh: 于是金、银、铜、铁、泥都一同砸得粉碎，成如夏天禾场上的糠秕，被风吹散，无处可寻。打碎这像的石头变成一座大山，充满天下。
verses.en: Then the iron, clay, bronze, silver, and gold were broken in pieces without distinction[NOTE:1] and became like chaff from the summer threshing floors that the wind carries away. Not a trace of them could be found. But the stone that struck the statue became a large mountain that filled the entire earth.
notes: Aram “as one.” For the meaning “without distinction” see the following: F. Rosenthal, Grammar, 36, §64, and p. 93; E. Vogt, Lexicon linguae aramaicae, 60.

verses.zh: 「这就是那梦。我们在王面前要讲解那梦。
verses.en: This was the dream. Now we[NOTE:1] will set forth before the king its interpretation.
notes: Various suggestions have been made concerning the plural “we.” It could be an editorial plural translatable as “I.” However, Daniel has portrayed himself as an agent of God, who revealed the matter (vv. 28, 30), so we can express that reality.

verses.zh: 王啊，你是诸王之王。天上的　神已将国度、权柄、能力、尊荣都赐给你。
verses.en: “You, O king, are the king of kings. The God of heaven has granted you sovereignty, power, strength, and honor.

verses.zh: 凡世人所住之地的走兽，并天空的飞鸟，他都交付你手，使你掌管这一切。你就是那金头。
verses.en: Wherever human beings,[NOTE:1] wild animals,[NOTE:2] and birds of the sky live—he has given them into your power.[NOTE:3] He has given you authority over them all. You are the head of gold.
notes: Aram “the sons of man.”
Aram “the beasts of the field.”
Aram “hand.”

verses.zh: 在你以后必另兴一国，不及于你；又有第三国，就是铜的，必掌管天下。
verses.en: Now after you another kingdom[NOTE:1] will arise, one inferior to yours. Then a third kingdom, one of bronze, will rule in all the earth.
notes: The identity of the first kingdom is clearly Babylon. The identification of the following three kingdoms is disputed. The common view is that they represent Media, Persia, and Greece. Most conservative scholars identify them as Media-Persia, Greece, and Rome.

verses.zh: 第四国，必坚壮如铁，铁能打碎克制百物，又能压碎一切，那国也必打碎压制列国。
verses.en: Then there will be a fourth kingdom, one strong like iron. Just like iron breaks in pieces and shatters everything, and as iron breaks in pieces[NOTE:1] all these metals,[NOTE:2] so it will break in pieces and crush the others.[NOTE:3]
notes: Theodotion and the Vulgate lack the phrase “and as iron breaks in pieces.”
The Aramaic text does not have this word, but it has been added in the translation for clarity.
The words “the others” are supplied from the context.

verses.zh: 你既见像的脚和脚指头，一半是窑匠的泥，一半是铁，那国将来也必分开。你既见铁与泥搀杂，那国也必有铁的力量。
verses.en: In that you were seeing feet and toes[NOTE:1] partly of wet clay[NOTE:2] and partly of iron, so this will be a divided kingdom. Some of the strength of iron will be in it, for you saw iron mixed with wet clay.[NOTE:3]
notes: The LXX lacks “and toes.”
Aram “potter’s clay.”
Aram “clay of clay” (also in v. 43).

verses.zh: 那脚指头，既是半铁半泥，那国也必半强半弱。
verses.en: In that the toes of the feet were partly of iron and partly of clay, the latter stages of this kingdom will be partly strong and partly fragile.

verses.zh: 你既见铁与泥搀杂，那国民也必与各种人搀杂，却不能彼此相合，正如铁与泥不能相合一样。
verses.en: And[NOTE:1] in that you saw iron mixed with wet clay, so people will be mixed[NOTE:2] with one another[NOTE:3] without adhering to one another, just as[NOTE:4] iron does not mix with clay.
notes: The present translation reads the conjunction, with most medieval Hebrew MSS, LXX, Vulgate, and the Qere. The Kethib lacks the conjunction.
The reference to people being mixed is usually understood to refer to intermarriage.
Aram “with the seed of men.”
The present translation reads הֵיךְ דִּי (hekh di) rather than the MT הֵא־כְדִי (heʾ khedi, “even as which”). It is a case of wrong word division.

verses.zh: 当那列王在位的时候，天上的　神必另立一国，永不败坏，也不归别国的人，却要打碎灭绝那一切国，这国必存到永远。
verses.en: In the days of those kings the God of heaven will raise up an everlasting kingdom that will not be destroyed and a kingdom that will not be left to another people. It will break in pieces and bring about the demise of all these kingdoms. But it will stand forever.

verses.zh: 你既看见非人手凿出来的一块石头从山而出，打碎金、银、铜、铁、泥，那就是至大的　神把后来必有的事给王指明。这梦准是这样，这讲解也是确实的。」
verses.en: You saw that a stone was cut from a mountain, but not by human hands; it smashed the iron, bronze, clay, silver, and gold into pieces. The great God has made known to the king what will occur in the future.[NOTE:1] The dream is certain, and its interpretation is reliable.”
notes: Aram “after this.”

verses.zh: 当时，尼布甲尼撒王俯伏在地，向但以理下拜，并且吩咐人给他奉上供物和香品。
verses.en: Then King Nebuchadnezzar bowed down with his face to the ground[NOTE:1] and paid homage to Daniel. He gave orders to offer sacrifice and incense to him.
notes: Aram “fell on his face.”

verses.zh: 王对但以理说：你既能显明这奥秘的事，你们的　神诚然是万神之神、万王之主，又是显明奥秘事的。」
verses.en: The king replied to Daniel, “Certainly your God is a God of gods and Lord of kings and revealer of mysteries, for you were able to reveal this mystery!”

verses.zh: 于是王高抬但以理，赏赐他许多上等礼物，派他管理巴比伦全省，又立他为总理，掌管巴比伦的一切哲士。
verses.en: Then the king elevated Daniel to high position and bestowed on him many marvelous gifts. He granted him authority over the entire province of Babylon and made him the main prefect over all the wise men of Babylon.

verses.zh: 但以理求王，王就派沙得拉、米煞、亚伯尼歌管理巴比伦省的事务，只是但以理常在朝中侍立。
verses.en: And at Daniel’s request, the king[NOTE:1] appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego over the administration of the province of Babylon. Daniel himself served in the king’s court.[NOTE:2]
notes: Aram “and Daniel sought from the king and he appointed.”
Aram “was at the gate of the king.”
